markdown_content: ## Overview of Grading OBJ Trims and Buttons in CLO This section explains how to grade OBJ trims and buttons in CLO, focusing on the importance of gluing trims, recognizing glued trims, and applying grading adjustments. It covers the process of selecting and positioning trims for grading, using the grading tool, and efficiently copying grading values across multiple buttons or buttonholes. --- ## Gluing OBJ Trims for Grading To grade OBJ trims (such as buttons or decorative elements), the trim must first be glued to the garment. Gluing a trim attaches it to a specific point on the pattern piece, which is essential for grading. ### Identifying Glued Trims - When a trim is glued, the glue bottle icon in the 2D window toolbar appears blue. - A small plus sign appears on the pattern piece, indicating the trim's gluing point. - If a trim is not glued, the glue bottle icon is unfilled (gray) and no plus sign appears. ### How to Glue a Trim 1. Select the trim in the 2D window. 2. Place the cursor at the desired gluing point on the trim. For example, the center of a button can be the gluing spot. 3. Click the glue bottle icon to activate gluing; the plus sign will appear on the pattern piece. 4. The trim is now glued and ready for grading. ### Adjusting or Removing Glue - To unglue a trim, right-click the trim and select "Unglue." - To move the gluing point, click the glue bottle icon again to deactivate, reposition the cursor, then reactivate gluing. - You can also rotate or adjust the trim’s position if needed before grading. --- ## Applying Grading to Glued OBJ Trims and Buttons Once trims are glued, grading can be assigned similarly to pattern pieces. ### Steps to Add Grading 1. Ensure your pattern pieces have grading already assigned. 2. Select the glued trim marker in the 2D window. 3. Open the grading tool in the grading section. 4. Use the arrow keys on your keyboard to incrementally add grading values (increasing or decreasing measurements). 5. Alternatively, input grading values directly in the measurements panel. 6. Repeat for other trims or buttons as needed. ### Grading Buttons and Buttonholes - Buttons placed using the button tool are automatically glued, so no manual gluing is required. - Select buttons or buttonholes and apply grading using the arrow keys or measurement inputs. --- ## Efficient Grading: Copying and Pasting Grading Values To streamline grading multiple trims, buttons, or buttonholes, CLO allows copying and pasting grading values across multiple items. ### Procedure for Copy-Pasting Grading 1. Right-click a graded trim or button and select "Copy." 2. Hold Shift and select multiple trims or buttons to apply the grading to. 3. Right-click and select "Paste," choosing from paste options: - Paste X and Y (both horizontal and vertical grading) - Paste X only - Paste Y only 4. Alternatively, use keyboard shortcuts: - Ctrl + C to copy - Ctrl + V to paste 5. This allows rapid and consistent grading application across multiple trims or buttonholes. --- ## Summary CLO now supports grading of OBJ trims and buttons by requiring trims to be glued first. The glue bottle icon and plus sign help identify glued trims. Grading adjustments can be made through arrow keys or measurement input, and grading values can be efficiently copied and pasted across multiple trims or buttons to save time and maintain consistency. This feature enhances precision and workflow efficiency in garment design and grading.
